=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions

**Scope:** The 16 issues you listed, reviewed against Wattlebridge's baseline: 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24m price, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. This is a negotiation analysis, not a final legal opinion. Items marked for confirmation need NSW counsel, privacy and tax specialists, and a check against the actual data room documents.

**Preliminary points on the Seller's cover note**

- **"FINAL / not to be re-opened":** Treat this as the Seller's opening position. Before accepting any claim that principals settled these terms, check our own record for a signed term sheet or agreed heads of terms.
- **"Market" ranges (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month limits):** These are asserted, not evidenced. I can't verify current market data, so don't adopt them as the benchmark.
- **Known quantified items:** Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 420k), Ironquay (AUD 180k open), and Sandbar (AUD 330k) total about AUD 4.13m. That is close to the Seller's entire AUD 4.8m general cap. These known items should be dealt with through the price mechanics and specific indemnities, not left to a capped general warranty claim.

---

## Priority order

1. **SPA-N-009, N-010:** Funds flow and debt-free mismatch
2. **SPA-N-008:** Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue)
3. **SPA-N-012:** Export/privacy incident (possible time-critical regulatory deadline)
4. **SPA-N-007, N-006, N-003, N-001, N-002, N-014:** Cap, threshold, time limit, disclosure and knowledge package
5. **SPA-N-011, N-015, N-004, N-005, N-016, N-013:** Remaining protections

---

## Risk allocation

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap as an opening counter, around 30–50% of price, with fundamentals and tax outside it. Known risks should sit in specific indemnities rather than the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** AUD 4.8m may be insufficient for the general warranty set, and known risks should be ring-fenced.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25k. Deductible basket AUD 250k (~1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 5–10k, with related claims aggregated. A tipping (first-dollar) basket of about 0.5% (~AUD 120k). Neither threshold applies to fundamentals, tax or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A deductible basket of AUD 250k means a AUD 240k loss recovers nothing; a tipping basket and lower de minimis preserve recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** General claims notified within 18 months of Completion. Any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3 / 13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties. Longer periods for fundamentals and tax. Specific indemnities run until the matter is resolved. Notified claims survive.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "applies to all Claims" default.** Known issues (Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy investigation) may not crystallise within 18 months.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares) outside the general cap and basket, capped at 100% of price, with a claims period of about 6 years.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title failure goes to what Wattlebridge is buying, so it cannot be treated as a general warranty.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing limits liability for fraud, with fraud defined. NSW law generally won't let a party exclude its own fraud, but express drafting avoids argument and should not be relied on alone.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; insert carve-out.** The wording captures deliberate misstatement and removes recourse for it.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single regime applies across general, fundamental, tax and IP matters.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories: general warranties; fundamentals; tax; IP. Specific indemnities for Bluefen, Ironquay, the export incident, bonuses and Riverlark, each with its own cap and time limit, outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject single regime.** It lets the general cap and short time limit absorb risks that are known and quantifiable.

---

## Disclosure and knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (to 22 Sept 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against specific warranties, fairly and fully described. No blanket disclosure of data room contents or public records. Disclosures must be reasonably apparent on their face.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Blanket data room disclosure makes most warranties meaningless, because Wattlebridge cannot tell what it has been deemed to know.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge does not affect warranty or indemnity claims, except for matters specifically and fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. The position under Australian law on this point isn't settled by default, so express drafting matters.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Combined with DL 1.1, this would turn every diligence finding, including the ten in this review, into a bar on recovery. Diligence is what the warranties are meant to back up.

---

## Specific transaction items

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2: no final consent, and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. FY26 revenue ~AUD 3.6m (~30%).
- **Buyer wants:** Consent and satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions as a condition precedent, waivable by Buyer, with a long-stop date. If waived: a specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue or termination, plus price retention or escrow. "All reasonable endeavours," with no payments or concessions to Bluefen without Buyer consent. A warranty that no termination notice has been received.
- **Recommendation:** **Escalate / Counter.** About 30% of revenue is exposed on change of control, and the Seller's drafting only requires the consent itself, not the cl 11.3 conditions.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2 / 7). DL 3: not repaid, no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** Under debt-free/cash-free, repay at Completion out of the price. Payoff letter and discharge of security (including PPSR release) delivered at Completion. Deduction in the funds flow. Warranty that no other security exists.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release.** Wattlebridge should not take the company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still outstanding. Debt is paid from proceeds, not left with the company.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5: conditional Completion bonuses, with no statement on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat as debt-like or Seller-borne. Include in the funds flow or deduct from the price. Include payroll tax, superannuation and other employer on-costs. Specific indemnity for all transaction-related employee payments. Confirm exactly who pays the bonuses and when.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** These are company liabilities that crystallise at or after Completion. If they are left out of the funds flow, Wattlebridge bears them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Described as "adequate." DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment. DD-010: AUD 180k open. No receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the general cap, covering all Ironquay claims: unpaid fees, IP ownership and infringement, third-party claims, and costs of recreating materials. Confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable. Payment of the AUD 180k by the Seller before Completion, or retention of that amount.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as "adequate."** A payment-only indemnity does not secure ownership of materials the company needs, and ownership depends on payment and an assignment that haven't been delivered.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Described as preliminary and "not expected to be material." DL 6: download link sent to an unintended external address. Up to ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Unknown whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. No loss amount stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Completed investigation before Completion, including a written assessment of notifiability under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) NDB scheme. Specific indemnity for all losses (notification, regulatory, third-party, forensic and remediation), outside the cap, basket and de minimis. Escrow or retention sized to the exposure. Warranty of no other incidents. Buyer participation in regulator communications.
- **Recommendation:** **Escalate.** "Not expected to be material" is not a finding. Personal information of roughly 1,240 people, unknown access, and an open notifiability question create live regulatory exposure. **Time-critical:** if the company has reasonable grounds to suspect an eligible data breach, the NDB assessment period is generally 30 days. Since the disclosure is dated 22 September and today is 5 November, that period may already have passed. Confirm urgently with privacy counsel, and confirm the company is an APP entity (likely, given revenue scale).

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate), described as ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8: no statement on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarify term, termination rights, change-of-control terms and whether any amounts are prepaid or accrued. Items relating to the pre-Completion period, or prepayments, should be treated as debt-like or adjusted in working capital. Interim covenant: no new supplier commitments outside the ordinary course without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter / clarify.** The "ordinary course" label is asserted, not shown, and the disclosure doesn't address terminability.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the share register (DD-012).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract; original share certificates and executed transfer forms; inspection of the statutory register; PPSR search for security over the shares; confirmation of no options or other equity instruments. Title warranty plus fundamental indemnity. Title confirmation as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** The register records the Seller's own position. It is not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties considered "settled under the general regime," meaning subject to the caps and short time limits, with nothing specific.
- **Buyer wants:** Full tax warranties, plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the cap and basket, running to the statutory amendment period, with Buyer conduct of audits. Full IP warranties covering ownership, registrations, non-infringement, open source, and employee and contractor assignments. Neither sits under the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Tax liabilities are often not discovered until ATO review, and an 18-month capped regime leaves Wattlebridge exposed.

---

## Remaining item

**SPA-N-014 (see above)** covers category separation. The remaining items are covered in the sections above.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. Confirm whether any signed term sheet exists before accepting "settled" positions.
2. Urgently confirm the privacy NDB position (SPA-N-012).
3. Require the Riverlark payoff, bonus treatment and Ironquay assignment in the funds flow before Completion.
4. Verify title independently (SPA-N-015).
5. Ask NSW counsel to confirm the fraud, sandbagging and limitation-period drafting points.
6. Send the Seller a mark-up addressing the cap, threshold, time, disclosure and knowledge package together. Negotiating them separately lets each one look reasonable on its own.

Items relating to the pre-Completion period, or prepayments, should be treated as debt-like or adjusted in working capital. Interim covenant: no new supplier commitments outside the ordinary course without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter / clarify.** The "ordinary course" label is asserted, not shown, and the disclosure doesn't address terminability.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the share register (DD-012).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract; original share certificates and executed transfer forms; inspection of the statutory register; PPSR search for security over the shares; confirmation of no options or other equity instruments. Title warranty plus fundamental indemnity. Title confirmation as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** The register records the Seller's own position. It is not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties considered "settled under the general regime," meaning subject to the caps and short time limits, with nothing specific.
- **Buyer wants:** Full tax warranties, plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the cap and basket, running to the statutory amendment period, with Buyer conduct of audits. Full IP warranties covering ownership, registrations, non-infringement, open source, and employee and contractor assignments. Neither sits under the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Tax liabilities are often not discovered until ATO review, and an 18-month capped regime leaves Wattlebridge exposed.
